observed.facings.png: Three facings side by side at one scale on a checkerboard. Each shows a heavy four-legged beast built entirely from banded grey-tan stone slabs, with thin orange glowing cracks between the plates. A ridge of upright slabs runs along the spine. South shows a blunt head straight on. East shows a long low side profile with a segmented tapering tail on the left and a small snouted head on the right. North shows the rump, haunches and the segmented tail pointing down at the camera. South looks slightly taller than the others.
observed.south.png: Front view. A low, broad head sits between massive shoulders. It has a heavy brow, two small deep-set eyes and a downturned, frowning mouth, so the face reads as stern and slightly humanoid, like a rock golem. Plates rise behind it to a peaked dorsal ridge. Four thick pillar legs end in blocky toes. Every plate shows horizontal grey and ochre strata bands, with orange glow at the seams near the shoulders and flanks. The background is clean transparency.
observed.east.png: Side profile facing right. The torso is long and barrel-shaped, made of rounded banded rock plates. Tall angular dorsal slabs peak over the shoulders and shrink toward the rear. A segmented conical tail tapers down to the left. The head on the right is small and low, wedge-snouted, with a small eye. The legs are thick and column-like. Orange glow shows at the plate seams. There are faint red fringe pixels on a few silhouette edges: the top of the dorsal slabs and the tail at the far left edge of the canvas, where the tail tip comes very close to the border.
observed.north.png: Rear view. Two large rounded haunches made of banded stone plates, with a segmented cone-shaped tail hanging down the middle. Two orange glowing seams sit either side of the tail root. The dorsal ridge rises to a peak above. Thick hind legs are in front and the forelegs show behind. There is no face and no eyes. A faint reddish fringe shows at the top tip.
observed.scale.png: At max zoom (128 px/cell) the beast's flank fills the frame beside a vanilla human, with the stone strata and glowing cracks crisp and detailed. In normal play (32 px/cell) the beast is many times the human's size and spans about 7 cells. It reads as a grey stone hulk with a spiked ridge, orange seam sparks and a clear silhouette against the sand.

NORTH_REAR.seen: North shows haunches and a downward-pointing segmented tail. No face or eyes.

NO_OVERHEAD.seen: All three are at the game's angled camera. None is a plan view.

SIGNATURE.seen: The banded mineral hide with heat glowing at the seams between plates is the dominant read on every facing.

ALIEN.seen: It reads as a living rock or mineral megabeast, not a tortoise or any Earth animal. Its nearest associations are fantasy (stone golem, ankylosaur) rather than an extant species.

DEPARTURES.seen: Line 1, banded hide of mineral, not skin or fur: present. Every surface is stratified stone plating with no skin or fur.

STYLE.seen: It is painterly-realistic sculpted stone with soft light and no keylines or cel shading. The south face is stern rather than cute, though somewhat humanoid and golem-like (see the polish finding).

OURS.seen: A bespoke design matching the description. Not a vanilla or other-mod animal.

ALPHA.seen: Real alpha with no ground, shadow or backdrop. There is only a faint red edge fringe on a few silhouette pixels in east and north (polish).

OWNER_NOTES.seen: Drawn at 7.5 cells. scale.png shows it as a true giant towering over the human. The Zeer is not shown, but 7.5 cells against the Zeer's 6 satisfies the note's size requirement.

SCALE.seen: Megafauna size beside the human fits 'migratory megafauna'.

LEGIBLE.seen: At 32 px/cell it reads as a few bold shapes: a grey hulk, a spiked dorsal ridge, pillar legs and orange sparks, all distinct from the sand.

request.subject: RM_FurnaceBeast

edits.change: The head is an animal head: a long, blunt muzzle built from banded stone plates, small dull dark wide-set eyes set into the sides of the head, and a closed jaw drawn as one plain straight seam of stone. The brow is a smooth, low, flat plate with no furrow, and the face carries the calm, blank look of a grazing animal.

Replace 'a heavy plated brow, and the mouth a straight, hard, closed line of stone, stern and never smiling' with 'a smooth low brow plate; the head is shaped like a big herbivore's head, with a wide stone muzzle and a closed jaw line'.

Every outer silhouette edge, including the dorsal slab tops, the ridge crest and the tail tip, is a clean dark-outlined stone edge, anti-aliased in the stone's own grey, tan and ochre tones. Orange and red glow appears only inside the narrow plate seams, set back from the outline and fully covered by the dark outline at the silhouette.

The whole animal, including the full tail tip, sits inside the canvas with a clear transparent margin of at least one tenth of the canvas width on the left and right, and the tail curves or hangs close to the body so that it ends well inside the frame.

invariants: Banded mineral plate hide with horizontal strata in cool grey, tan and ochre stone; not skin or fur
Glowing ember orange-yellow seams between plates, brightest at shoulder, flank and haunch, dimmer deep red elsewhere
Colossal, broad, deep-chested body on exactly four thick columnar pillar legs with broad flat feet
Dorsal ridge of plates peaking above the shoulder; small head carried low
Underbelly of smaller interlocking stone plates with glowing seams
Painterly vanilla RimWorld style, soft hand-painted plate forms, clean dark outline, transparent background
One fixed scale, every foot complete inside the canvas
request.prompt: A realistic, painterly vanilla RimWorld-style sprite of the furnace-beast, a colossal migratory megafauna, the largest animal on its world, that reads as a huge mineral mass on legs, like a walking stone kiln the size of a house, on a transparent background with a clean dark outline. Its hide is made of separate, weighty stone-like mineral plates, not continuous skin, banded in visible horizontal strata of differing mineral colours across the whole body: cool grey, tan and ochre stone on the plate faces. The surfaces are painted in the soft, hand-painted manner of vanilla RimWorld sprites: broad shaded plate forms with flat tonal blocks, texture used sparingly on a few plates only, and softly rounded plate edges. The cracks and seams between the plates glow a warm ember orange-yellow like coals showing through gaps in a stove: narrow lines with a gentle inner light, bright yellow-orange at a few joints (shoulder, flank, haunch) and dimmer deep red elsewhere, so the beast reads as hot inside at a glance while the stone plates carry the image. The only strong orange on the body is this heat inside the plate joints; the plates themselves stay cool stone, and the glow sits set back from the outer silhouette, fully covered by the dark outline at the edge. The underbelly is covered in smaller interlocking stone plates with glowing seams and visible strata, so every part of the body shows stone plate. The body is enormous, broad and deep-chested, much heavier than any grazing animal. There are exactly four legs, one at each corner of the body: very thick, straight, columnar stone pillars like the legs of the very largest land giants, short relative to the depth of the body, with broad flat feet, plated, with heated joints matching the body. The body plan, proportions and palette stay consistent throughout, with the tail and haunches built from the same heavy plates. The head is an animal head, small relative to the huge body and carried low: a long, blunt, wide muzzle built from banded stone plates like a big herbivore's head, a smooth low flat brow plate, small, dull, dark eyes set wide apart on the sides of the head, and a closed jaw drawn as one plain straight seam of stone, with the calm, blank expression of a grazing animal. It is one full-height animal with a long body, standing tall on straight pillar legs with a high back and a dorsal ridge of plates that peaks above the shoulder. The crown plate, the dorsal slab tops, the ridge crest, the tail tip and every outer plate edge end in clean, crisp stone edges against fully transparent background, anti-aliased in the stone's own grey, tan and ochre tones, with opaque pixels right up to the dark outline and nothing floating outside it. The tail hangs close to the body and ends well inside the frame. The plates are cold, hard rock: chipped and fractured edges, granular mineral grain and a dusting of grey ash, never wood grain or bark. The animal is drawn at one fixed scale with a clear transparent margin of at least one tenth of the canvas width on every side, the full tail tip and every foot complete inside the canvas.
